note: Hand-curated. Town records (minutes, resolutions, meeting transcripts) are marked 'town'; news coverage is marked 'news' and is not a Town record. Machine transcripts can mishear words. Checked by web/scripts/verify-supervisor-addresses.mjs.

governor.text: The governor shall communicate by message to the legislature at every session the condition of the state, and recommend such matters to it as he or she shall judge expedient.
governor.cite: New York State Constitution, Article IV, § 3

townReport.text: Town Law § 29(10) requires the supervisor to file an annual financial report with the town clerk within thirty days after the fiscal year ends; under § 29(10-a) a town board may instead have the supervisor file a copy of the annual report sent to the State Comptroller.
townReport.cite: New York Town Law § 29, subdivisions 10 and 10-a

law.finding: This site found no State law that requires a town supervisor to give a 'State of the Town' address or an inaugural speech. In Riverhead both are customs.

format.before2018: Before 2018 the address was given at a joint dinner meeting of the Riverhead Rotary, Kiwanis and Lions clubs, held at local restaurants.
format.change2018: Laura Jens-Smith moved it to Town Hall in 2018, free to attend, broadcast on the public-access channel and livestreamed.

source.title: RiverheadLOCAL, March 18, 2019: Jens-Smith announces 'State of the Town' address at town hall April 8

supervisors.name: Sean Walter

inauguration.summary: Took office on January 1, 2010, setting out three goals: fiscal health, downtown revitalization and redeveloping the Enterprise Park at Calverton (EPCAL).

sources.title: RiverheadLOCAL, December 31, 2017: A look back at eight years of Sean Walter

addresses.where: Joint dinner of the Rotary, Kiwanis and Lions clubs
addresses.summary: His first address; he gave one every year through 2016, each restating his three goals.

sources.title: RiverheadLOCAL, December 31, 2017: A look back at eight years of Sean Walter

addresses.where: Joint meeting of the Riverhead Kiwanis, Rotary and Lions clubs
addresses.summary: Proposed merging the elected tax receiver into the Town Clerk's office and replacing the elected Board of Assessors with appointed assessors, which he said would save $150,000 a year, and one combined highway, garage and State DOT yard at EPCAL to save another $150,000. He predicted the first proposal would "be met with an uproar."

sources.title: RiverheadLOCAL, February 25, 2015: Walter in 'State of Town' to call for elimination of elected tax receiver, assessor positions

addresses.summary: His last address, recorded on video.

gaps: No address in 2017, his final year.
Walter was re-elected three times; this site has not found coverage of his 2012, 2014 and 2016 swearing-ins, so the timeline marks only 2010.

inauguration.summary: Sworn in as the Town's 62nd Supervisor and its first woman in the office; called for unity, cooperation and perseverance in Town government.

inauguration.summary: Sworn in as the 63rd Supervisor at the Suffolk Theater, the only official that day to give a speech, urging residents to work together rather than rely on government alone. At the next Board meeting she said "We had over two, three hundred and fifty people at the theater." Sworn in for a second term on January 2, 2022 at a scaled-back ceremony at Town Hall, with a seven-minute prepared address.

supervisors.name: Jerome (Jerry) Halpin

inauguration.summary: Sworn in as the 65th Supervisor at a packed Town Hall. His first salary resolution set the Supervisor's 2026 pay at $110,000, "reduced from budgeted amount of $118,919." At the January 6 meeting he twice pointed back to the speech, saying it would be "a little clunky at first" and that "we could look for the negative in everything."
